name: Iron and Wax
gmNotes:
Investigation Side Mission: mystery, sensory impairment, folklore/science clues, comic danger, social correction, and home warmth. Playable before or after Cream Tax and Milk and Feathers. Do not identify the workshop's iron or horseshoes before the team enters; Coinin does not know the cause, and Buaic can only suspect iron if asked. Read Fey Origins, Biology and Senses for iron effects; symptoms now, full magnetoception explanation later, Roman Iron Flood connection only at its protected reveal. Do not expose the laboratory supply chain, Fey no-lie rule, Morrigan's human origin, staged rescue, Rory/Yror objective, or Meabh's assignment.

The apprentice stole village threshold horseshoes to protect himself from Morrigan. The thefts contributed to the village lockdown. He promises to return them soon, not instantly: this mission does not remove Cream Tax's watch. His rumours foreshadow later truths: raven/wolf appearances and animal speech are glamoured drone relays; simultaneous appearances are remote presence; ownership means service/indenture. 'She's a liar' is literally true but its significance stays hidden. These are GM-only explanations, not Meabh's early answers.

Each obstacle is distinct; never collapse the mission into one search roll or demand a roll per horseshoe. Roll only for meaningful uncertainty with a named Condition at risk; apply Checks and Conditions and One Obstacle, One Roll. Humans, including Meabh, do not share Fey iron toxicity. A thrown horseshoe can injure anyone physically, but only actual Fey suffer the alien sensory/toxic effects.
briefing: Coinin knows a Brownie candle-maker who cannot use his workshop and needs human help. Buaic has honey, but any exchange must be negotiated with him.
objective: Discover what is keeping Buaic from his workshop and negotiate for the honey owed to Coinin.
debriefing: Buaic is back among his candles, Grannie has a wax light fit for a feast day, and Coinin has his honey. If the separate cream and milk obligations are also fulfilled, your side of the bargain is complete.

storyBeats.title: A Brownie in Need
storyBeats.events: Coinin sends the team to Buaic, a Brownie who normally makes candles at the widowed beekeeper's workshop by night. Something in or around it prevents him entering. He needs human help and can provide honey, but Coinin has not negotiated payment. The concealed Fairy Door offers a route to the western woods near the workshop.
storyBeats.objective: Hear Coinin's proposal for obtaining the honey.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Coinin knows the problem, not its cause: no iron or horseshoe explanation. He neither owns nor promises Buaic's honey. Keep the supply chain hidden. Let the team use the Fairy Door to the Hidden Fairy Door or another sensible route; this bypasses travel, not the obstacles.

storyBeats.title: The Finest Candles in the Region
storyBeats.events: Around nightfall, Buaic waits outside the bee skeps, angry, nauseated and disoriented. He cannot trust paths, sides or distances near the workshop: parts of it feel absent. 'There's too much of something in there. The room is wrong.' Asked how, he reluctantly compares it to the Iron Flood: 'Almost a bit like what they say about the Iron Flood. Sure, it doesn't flow, it doesn't flood whole landscapes, it doesn't leave patterns behind, but still…' Then: 'I've already said too much. We don't talk about the Iron Flood.'
storyBeats.objective: Hear Buaic's symptoms and agree how to help.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Unlock Brownie Common Knowledge. Respect his professional pride and real impairment. He refuses further Iron Flood details; no Rome, armies, northward sense or active ping explanation. If the player suggests iron, he admits it is plausible, not confirmed. Before approaching the skeps, offer a separate bargain: 'If you remove whatever is preventing me from safely using my workshop, I will give you two measures of honey.' Let the team accept or negotiate. On acceptance, create Buaic's Workshop bargain with the accepting team and Buaic, record exact agreed wording and each obligation, and present the document handout per Grace, Language and Bargains. Do not pre-create acceptance or merge this with Coinin's Silence. 'Coinin does not own my honey. He has not bargained for me.'

storyBeats.title: Past the Skeps
storyBeats.events: The approach passes the bee skeps. Animals, Nature, Food, sensible smoke, patience or another sound plan can avoid or reduce disturbance.
storyBeats.objective: Pass the bee skeps without provoking them.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Keep the obstacle light. A minor disturbance or single sting may cause 1 Nerve Depletion; a swarm or badly mishandled hive may cause 1 Health Depletion. Choose the fitting consequence, not both automatically. Safe clever handling needs no roll. Apply the normal critical limits; never make this lethal or a dead end.

storyBeats.title: Something Among the Wax
storyBeats.events: Inside are tools, wax, benches and shelves—and iron. Horseshoes lie openly across the floor and are tucked into thresholds, tools and wax stores. The quantity and placement are deliberate. The apprentice sleeps in or near the workshop clutching one more.
storyBeats.objective: Enter the workshop and identify what has changed.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Reveal the iron and then the horseshoes through inspection, not a gatekeeping roll. A protagonist with smith training recognises familiar village work and threshold protection; other protagonists can read the deliberate placement and protective intent plainly. Leave the theft connection for the player to make. Meabh can explain that contact hurts Fey and dense iron disrupts their directional/spatial sense, making places feel wrong or missing. No full scientific lecture or Roman connection.

storyBeats.title: Horseshoes in the Dark
storyBeats.events: The team gathers obvious and concealed horseshoes while the apprentice sleeps. Buaic gives feedback from a safe distance as the iron is carried away: 'Better. The left side of the room exists again.' Later: 'There—I can feel the doorway now.' The last horseshoe remains in the apprentice's hand.
storyBeats.objective: Remove the scattered iron without startling the apprentice.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: No fixed horseshoe count. Iron, smithcraft and observation can help find caches; roll only if noise or another meaningful risk matters. A missed cache or noise leads to feedback or the apprentice waking, not repeated identical checks. Move collected iron away from Buaic and the entrance. Do not set workshop-cleared until the final horseshoe is removed and he can safely enter.

storyBeats.title: The Queen in the Stories
storyBeats.events: The apprentice wakes, or is gently woken, so the last horseshoe can be relinquished. Startling him may cause panic and thrown horseshoes. He fears Morrigan specifically: 'She turns into a raven'; 'She turns into a wolf'; 'She can be in two places at once'; 'She watches through animals'; 'She owns people'; 'She's a liar.' He took the horseshoes to protect himself and the workshop.
storyBeats.objective: Persuade the apprentice to surrender the last horseshoe and return the stolen protections.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Use a few rumours naturally, not a checklist. Keep him sympathetic. Meabh takes his fear seriously: 'She does not turn into a raven.' 'So there is a raven?' She says nothing. At 'liar', she reacts sharply: 'Who told you that?' or 'That is a dangerous thing to say about a Queen.' No explanation of why. She may disclose 'She owns my service. Which is near enough to owning me,' but no details of her assignment. Discuss domestic Fey not all being alike, theft, unprotected households and the strengthened watch. When the player connects the cache to missing village horseshoes, he confesses. He takes the horseshoes away and promises to return them 'soon'; do not clear the village lockdown. Resolve panic through another approach if needed. Set workshop-cleared to 1 only once Buaic can enter safely.

storyBeats.title: Honey and a Candle
storyBeats.events: Buaic enters normally at last, relieved and genuinely happy to have his bench back. He pays the agreed two measures of honey and separately gives one fine wax candle: 'The honey is payment. The candle is for your Grannie. She's a kind woman. Or so I've heard.' Set honey to 2 and wax-candle to 1 when received.
storyBeats.objective: Restore Buaic's work and receive the promised payment.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Resolve the team's workshop obligation when access is restored and Buaic's honey obligation when paid; resolve Buaic's Workshop once both are fulfilled. Honour any negotiated wording. The candle is an additional personal gift, not contract payment or a new condition. Apply normal courtesy rules if relevant without manufacturing a dispute or withholding rewards. Unlock Brownie Deep Lore through the exchange: Brownies and Hobs normally work for humans at night in return for food, cream or milk; Buaic is not usually the one hiring humans. Do not reveal who consumes those supplies. 'Or so I've heard' hints at Pantry Hob gossip without explaining it. Contrast his genuine generosity with Coinin's opportunism.

storyBeats.title: The Last Measures
storyBeats.events: The team brings two measures of honey back to Coinin's Hollow Tree. He acknowledges delivery. The accepting party's honey obligation is now complete; if the cream and milk have also been delivered, all three goods obligations are complete. Coinin remains bound not to tell Morrigan that he saw them together.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Keep the honey tracker at target as historical objective progress. In Coinin's Silence, resolve the accepting party's honey obligation independently. Do not alter the cream or milk obligations and do not resolve Coinin's ongoing nondisclosure obligation.

storyBeats.title: Waxlight
storyBeats.events: The player brings Grannie the fine wax candle. She is genuinely delighted: 'Oh my, a wax candle! Like a noble woman! I'll save it for a special occasion…'
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Close with home warmth, not another explanation or payment demand. Preserve the candle tracker at target as history.

description: Something in the beekeeper's workshop has made it unbearable to its nocturnal candle-maker. Investigate the strange disturbance and help Buaic recover his bench.
completionEffects: Verify Buaic's Workshop has its fulfilled clearance and honey-payment obligations resolved. Honey delivery independently resolves only the accepting party's honey obligation in Coinin's Silence; leave cream, milk and Coinin's ongoing nondisclosure unchanged. Preserve trackers at target as history. The apprentice's promised returns do not instantly lift the village watch. Do not advance the moon phase.
